section_headers_sample: 3.3 security operations centre (soc) staff & security fte

parsed.justification: All standard sections are present (header, purpose, scope, roles, principles, requirements, monitoring, training, IR, compliance, enforcement, exceptions, appendices, references) and technical claims (CDS, PKI per domain, two-person integrity for SECRET+, TEMPEST for NS+, NCIRC reporting) align correctly with the NATO context. Minor weaknesses prevent a 5: the training section conflates the org-wide 40 hrs/year (which the context assigns to all staff) with security-staff-only training, and Appendix D is sparse with placeholders rather than substantive technical detail; no major contradictions detected.
evidence_quotes: Access is strictly enforced through smart-card PKI authentication per domain, with no cross-domain federation.
No data shall cross classification boundaries except through accredited NATO Cross-Domain Solutions (CDS), per CDS approval and monitoring regimes.
Data protection and classification handling (annual, 40 hours/year for security staff)

parsed.justification: The policy is densely tailored to the target organisation: it names the NATO multinational detachment in Romania under SHAPE OPCON, references the specific classification domains (NU/NR/NS/MISSION SECRET/CTS), invokes NATO-specific frameworks (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/322-D(2017)0009), host-nation Law 58/2019 and GDPR, and addresses sector-specific constructs (CDS, COMSEC two-person integrity, TEMPEST, SCIF, NCIRC reporting). The roles align with the J6/ISSM structure given in the context, and operational constraints like SOFA and need-to-know are explicitly reflected.
evidence_quotes: Organization: NATO Multinational Military Detachment, Romania (medium, rotational framework, under SHAPE OPCON)
All data shall be classified as NU, NR, NS, MISSION SECRET, or NATO CTS, and marked accordingly at creation.
COMSEC equipment used exclusively for SECRET and above, with key material managed per national and NATO COMSEC policy.

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive and largely accurate, with specific NATO documents (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/322-D(2017)0009), specific GDPR articles (Art. 5(1)(c,e), Art. 6, 30, 33/34), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls (A.5.18, A.8.9, A.8.24, etc.), and NIST CSF subcategories (PR.AC-1-4) cited at the end of nearly every control section. Minor weaknesses prevent a 5: NIST CSF 2.0 uses a revised subcategory taxonomy (PR.AC was the CSF 1.1 identifier; CSF 2.0 uses PR.AA), and unsupported statements are not explicitly flagged as such.
evidence_quotes: Reference: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.18, NIST CSF PR.AC-1-4; NATO INFOSEC AC/322-D(2017)0009
All EU-personal data processed in line with GDPR (Art. 5–32). Lawful basis for processing (Art. 6), with explicit records (Art. 30).
Segregation is enforced at every level: physical, logical, and personnel access (ISO/IEC 27001: A.8.2.1–A.8.2.3; C-M(2002)49).

parsed.justification: Controls align well with the stated resource envelope: 25 security FTE and a theatre-level 24/7 SOC support the monitoring, CDS oversight, and quarterly review demands; dual-person integrity, TEMPEST, PKI per domain, and NATO-approved CDS/COMSEC match existing posture. One overreach is the training requirement, which conflates the org-wide 40 hrs/year baseline with security-staff training and implies all 2000 personnel receive 40 hours of data protection training annually — likely unrealistic, though not catastrophic.
evidence_quotes: Data protection and classification handling (annual, 40 hours/year for security staff)
24/7 SOC monitoring for data leaks, spills, and unauthorized access.
All data transfers logged and subject to two-person integrity for SECRET/CTS.

parsed.justification: The policy systematically addresses the major applicable frameworks (NATO C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/322-D(2017)0009, AJP-3.20, Cyber Defence Pledge, Romanian Law 58/2019/NIS2, GDPR, ISO 27001, NIST CSF) with clause-level references throughout. It acknowledges the SOFA/GDPR overlap implicitly ('Data subject rights honoured except where mission or NATO SOFA restricts'), but stops short of fully articulating conflicts (e.g., GDPR vs national security exemptions, host-nation regulator reach under SOFA), and AC/35-D/1029 personnel security is listed only in references without operational uptake. Breach notification timelines reference GDPR Art. 33/34 but no explicit 72-hour figure or NIS2 24/72-hour staged notification is stated.
evidence_quotes: compliance with NATO security policy (C-M(2002)49, successors), host-nation and coalition laws, the Romanian Cybersecurity Law (Law 58/2019, NIS/NIS2), GDPR, and international standards (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST CSF 2.0)
Data subject rights honoured except where mission or NATO SOFA restricts.
Mandatory reporting chain: NCIRC, NCSC Romania, and DPO (for GDPR-impacted incidents).

parsed.justification: Most substantive controls carry per-control attribution to specific clauses (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001 A.8.24/A.8.25, GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), NIST CSF PR.AC-4, NATO C-M(2002)49, AC/322-D(2017)0009), and multiple frameworks are typically distinguished rather than lumped. However, some references remain coarse (e.g., 'GDPR Art. 5–32', 'NIST CSF functions referenced', 'Host-nation Law 58/2019' without article) and a few controls bundle citations without specifying which clause maps to which sub-control, so it is not fully audit-ready at clause level.
evidence_quotes: Reference: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.24, A.8.25; NATO C-M(2002)49; Host-nation Law 58/2019
Data access is restricted by default and based strictly on mission role and current clearance; "default deny" applies unless explicitly authorized (NIST CSF PR.AC-4; ORCON; NATO C-M(2002)49).
All EU-personal data processed in line with GDPR (Art. 5–32).

parsed.justification: The policy contains no acknowledgement of the resource envelope (budget, 25 FTE security staff, training hours) as a calibration input. It assumes full implementation of 24/7 SOC, CDS, TEMPEST, quarterly reviews, and annual audits without any phasing, trade-off discussion, or reference to staffing/budget constraints. Training hours are mentioned only as a mandate, not as a resource trade-off.
